hints: Sort the four numbers into two pairs first. Which two chambers only have to push blood into the ventricles next door, and which two have to push blood out of the heart?

Remember where the two ventricles pump to. The left ventricle pumps all the way round the body, the right ventricle only pumps a short distance to the lungs, so which needs the huge pressure and which needs a medium pressure?
walkthrough:
**Separate atria from ventricles**

Think like a teacher with the heart in front of you. Atria only contract gently to push blood a very short distance down into the ventricles.

So the two lowest maximum pressures, $3 \text{ mm Hg}$ and $10 \text{ mm Hg}$, must belong to the right and left atria.

**Compare the two ventricles**

Ventricles do the hard work of pushing blood out of the heart. The left ventricle pumps to the whole body through the aorta, so it needs a very thick wall and generates a very high pressure.

The right ventricle only pumps to the lungs through the pulmonary artery, which is very close by, so it needs much less pressure than the left.

**Assign the numbers**

The highest value, $120 \text{ mm Hg}$, must be the powerful left ventricle. That leaves the intermediate value.

Therefore the right ventricle, stronger than either atrium but much weaker than the left ventricle, is $25 \text{ mm Hg}$.

options.A: Too low for a ventricle. This is an atrial pressure, the very gentle push from an atrium into a ventricle.
options.B: Still too low for a ventricle. This is the other atrial pressure, slightly higher on the left side but not a pumping-out-of-heart pressure.
options.C: Correct. This medium pressure fits the right ventricle, strong enough to send blood to the nearby lungs but much lower than the left ventricle.
options.D: Too high for the right side. This is the left ventricle pressure needed to drive blood around the whole body.
